pathogen: Alternaria solani (Fungus that causes dark concentric ring spots)
symptoms: Brown or dark spots with concentric ring patterns appear on older leaves.
Yellow rings surround the dark spots as the surrounding tissue weakens.
Leaves can turn yellow, dry up, and drop off early if the disease spreads.
Dark sunken spots may develop on stems near the soil level.
causes: Warm and humid weather (24–29°C) combined with wet leaves from rain or sprinkler watering.
Fungus spores surviving in infected old plant residue or soil weeds.
spread: Spreads through splashing water droplets, heavy morning dew, and wind carrying fungal spores.
preventive_measures: Rotate crops every 2-3 years with non-tomato plants (such as corn or beans).
Water at the base of the plant using drip irrigation to keep leaves dry.
Stake and prune plants to improve airflow and keep leaves off wet soil.
Place clean straw or mulch around plant bases to prevent soil splashing onto leaves.
organic_treatments: Spray copper-based organic soap spray at the first sign of lower leaf spotting.
Apply bio-fungicides containing beneficial Bacillus subtilis bacteria.
Spray mild neem oil solution (0.5%) mixed with baking soda water.
chemical_controls: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g per litre of water as a preventive protective spray.
Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g per litre of water at 7–10 day intervals during wet periods.
Curative fungicides such as Difenoconazole or Azoxystrobin if infection is spreading rapidly.

pathogen: Phytophthora infestans (Water mold fungus that causes rapid leaf rotting)
symptoms: Dark, water-soaked, irregular brown blotches form on leaf edges and spread quickly.
A delicate white fuzzy fungal growth appears on leaf undersides on humid mornings.
Stems and leaf stalks turn dark brown to greasy black.
Whole leaves collapse and rot rapidly in cool, rainy weather.
causes: Cool, wet weather (15–22°C) with high humidity above 90%.
Infected seed tubers or airborne spores blown from nearby potato or tomato fields.
spread: Spreads rapidly through windblown moisture droplets and fog across miles.
preventive_measures: Plant resistant tomato varieties when available.
Remove self-sprouted volunteer tomato or potato plants before planting.
Avoid evening overhead watering to ensure foliage dries before nighttime.
Remove and safely dispose of infected plants immediately (do not compost them).
organic_treatments: Spray Bordeaux mixture (1% copper sulfate and lime) as a protective cover.
Apply copper hydroxide spray before forecasted heavy rains.
Foliar spray with Trichoderma harzianum beneficial fungus.
chemical_controls: Metalaxyl-M + Mancozeb (Ridomil Gold) @ 2.5g per litre of water.
Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g per litre of water.
Dimethomorph 50% WP @ 1g per litre of water for strong protective action.

pathogen: None (Healthy Plant)
symptoms: Leaves have an even, healthy green color with clear leaf veins.
No brown or yellow disease spots, powdery films, or rot are present.
Leaf margins are smooth and firm with normal growth.
causes: Optimal growing conditions with balanced soil nutrition, moisture, and sunlight.
spread: Not applicable (healthy plant).
preventive_measures: Maintain balanced watering and avoid waterlogged soil.
Apply balanced fertilizer with adequate calcium to prevent blossom rot.
Scout plants weekly to catch any early disease signs.
organic_treatments: Foliar seaweed extract spray can help support natural plant immunity.
chemical_controls: No chemical sprays needed for healthy plants.

pathogen: Alternaria solani (Fungus that causes circular brown leaf spots)
symptoms: Dark brown spots with concentric ring rings appear first on lower leaves.
Leaves surrounding the spots turn yellow, dry out, and curl up.
Early leaf loss reduces the plant's ability to grow large tubers.
causes: Alternating dry and humid weather cycles (24–30°C).
Plant stress caused by low nitrogen or drought.
spread: Fungal spores spread by wind and water splashing from the soil.
preventive_measures: Use certified disease-free seed potatoes.
Rotate fields with non-potato crops (like maize or beans) every 3 years.
Provide balanced fertilizer to keep plants vigorous during tuber growth.
organic_treatments: Spray copper oxychloride 50% WP when first leaf spots appear.
Apply beneficial Bacillus bacteria bio-fungicides.
chemical_controls: Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g per litre of water as protective spray.
Propineb 70% WP @ 2g per litre.
Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.5 mL per litre for curative treatment.

pathogen: Phytophthora infestans (Fungus-like water mold causing black rot)
symptoms: Dark, water-soaked brown-black patches spread rapidly across leaf tips.
White mold appears on the underside of affected leaves in damp mornings.
Infected fields may develop a rotting smell as foliage breaks down.
Tubers can develop dry brown rot under the skin if spores wash into soil.
causes: Cool, damp weather with humidity above 90% and temperatures around 12–20°C.
Infected seed potatoes harboring overwintering mold.
spread: Airborne spores carried on moist wind currents and rain runoff.
preventive_measures: Hill up soil around potato ridges to prevent spores from reaching tubers.
Destroy cull piles and self-grown volunteer potato plants.
Mow down potato haulms 10 days before harvest to protect tuber skins.
organic_treatments: Spray copper hydroxide before predicted rainy periods.
Natural horsetail or silica-rich plant extracts.
chemical_controls: Cymoxanil + Mancozeb @ 2g per litre of water.
Mandipropamid 23.4% SC @ 0.8 mL per litre.
Fluopicolide + Propamocarb for severe disease pressure.

pathogen: None (Healthy Plant)
symptoms: Deep emerald-green foliage with smooth leaf margins and clear veins.
No dark blight spots, curling edges, or signs of mold.
causes: Good field management, healthy seed tubers, and balanced moisture.
spread: Not applicable (healthy plant).
preventive_measures: Scout weekly for any signs of early or late blight.
Keep soil evenly moist without waterlogging.
organic_treatments: Apply mild organic compost tea to support leaf health.
chemical_controls: No chemical treatment needed.

pathogen: Puccinia sorghi (Fungus that produces reddish-brown powdery rust spores)
symptoms: Small oval cinnamon-brown powdery pustules appear scattered on both leaf surfaces.
Pustules break open and release reddish-brown powdery spores.
Leaves turn yellow and dry up when many pustules join together.
Extensive leaf damage reduces kernel filling in corn ears.
causes: Moderate temperatures (16–25°C) with high humidity and prolonged dew on leaves.
Rust spores blown northwards on seasonal winds.
spread: Airborne spores carried long distances on wind and settling on moist corn leaves.
preventive_measures: Plant rust-resistant corn hybrid seeds when available.
Plant early in the season to avoid peak spore migration times.
Avoid over-fertilizing with nitrogen, which produces overly soft leaves.
organic_treatments: Spray wettable sulfur (80% WDG) @ 3g per litre at early signs of rust.
Neem oil solution (1%) foliar spray to reduce spore germination.
chemical_controls: Azoxystrobin + Propiconazole @ 1 mL per litre of water.
Tebuconazole 25.9% EC @ 1 mL per litre applied around the tasseling stage.

pathogen: Exserohilum turcicum (Fungus causing long cigar-shaped blights)
symptoms: Long, cigar-shaped grayish-green to tan lesions (2 to 15 cm long) on leaves.
Lesions develop dark fuzzy mold on undersides during humid weather.
Large blighted areas join together and cause whole corn leaves to dry up.
causes: Moderate temperatures (18–27°C) with extended leaf wetness from rain or dew.
Fungus surviving in leftover corn stalks on the soil surface.
spread: Spores blown by wind from old crop stubble onto lower leaves.
preventive_measures: Choose resistant corn hybrids.
Plow under corn crop residue after harvest to help debris decompose.
Rotate corn with non-grass crops like soybeans or small grains.
organic_treatments: Bio-fungicides containing Bacillus bacteria.
Preventive copper spray before the silking stage.
chemical_controls: Pyraclostrobin + Fluxapyroxad @ 0.5 mL per litre of water.
Trifloxystrobin + Tebuconazole @ 0.7g per litre.

pathogen: None (Healthy Plant)
symptoms: Bright, uniform green parallel-veined leaves with sturdy midribs.
No rust pustules, tan streaks, or dead leaf margins.
causes: Good soil nutrients, adequate moisture, and clean planting stock.
spread: Not applicable (healthy plant).
preventive_measures: Test soil fertility and ensure balanced nitrogen, phosphorus, and zinc.
Monitor canopy during tasseling and silking.
organic_treatments: Apply foliar micronutrient spray if required.
chemical_controls: No chemical treatment needed.

pathogen: Venturia inaequalis (Fungus causing dark velvety scab spots)
symptoms: Olive-green to velvety dark brown-black circular spots appear on leaves.
Spots turn rough and cork-like as they mature.
Affected leaves curl, turn yellow, and drop off early.
Rough, dark cracked scabs can develop on apple fruits.
causes: Wet spring weather with continuous leaf moisture (9+ hours wetness at 10–20°C).
Fungal spores released from fallen leaves on the orchard floor.
spread: Rain and wind splash spores from fallen dead leaves onto new spring buds and leaves.
preventive_measures: Plant scab-resistant apple cultivars.
Rake and shred fallen autumn leaves or apply compost to speed up leaf breakdown.
Prune orchard branches to allow sunlight and wind to dry leaves quickly.
organic_treatments: Apply lime sulfur spray during the green tip and pink bud stages.
Potassium bicarbonate spray as a gentle eradicant.
chemical_controls: Captan 50% WP @ 2.5g per litre or Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2g per litre.
Difenoconazole 25% EC @ 0.3 mL per litre for curative action.

pathogen: Botryosphaeria obtusa (Fungus causing frogeye spots and fruit rot)
symptoms: Small purple specks on leaves expand into circular tan spots with purple edges (frogeye shape).
Dead bark cankers form on tree limbs.
Infected fruit turns black, shrivels, and remains hanging as dried mummies.
causes: Fungus overwintering in dead branches, bark cankers, and dried mummified fruit.
Warm temperatures (20–27°C) accompanied by spring rains.
spread: Rain washes spores from infected cankers down to leaves and developing apples.
preventive_measures: Prune out dead wood, cankers, and remove all mummified apples during winter.
Maintain tree health to resist bark damage.
organic_treatments: Apply copper sulfate dormant spray before buds swell in spring.
chemical_controls: Captan 80% WDG @ 1.8g per litre.
Thiophanate-methyl 70% WP @ 1g per litre.

pathogen: None (Healthy Plant)
symptoms: Lustrous dark green leaves with serrated edges and clean surfaces.
causes: Good orchard pruning, clean floor management, and balanced tree nutrition.
spread: Not applicable (healthy plant).
preventive_measures: Continue annual pruning and routine orchard scouting.
organic_treatments: Apply organic seaweed extract during leaf growth.

pathogen: Guignardia bidwellii (Fungus causing circular brown leaf spots and fruit rot)
symptoms: Small circular reddish-brown spots with dark borders appear on leaves.
Tiny black specks form inside the leaf spots.
Infected grape berries turn dark, shrivel, and become hard, wrinkled black mummies.
causes: Warm and rainy weather (20–27°C) with prolonged moisture on leaves and berries.
Old dried mummified grapes left hanging on the trellis from last season.
spread: Raindrops splash fungal spores from old mummies onto young leaves and shoots.
preventive_measures: Remove and destroy all dried mummified grapes and prune infected canes in winter.
Thin the vine canopy to allow sun and air to dry leaves quickly.
organic_treatments: Apply copper-based sprays from early bloom until berries mature.
Lime sulfur dormant spray in late winter.
chemical_controls: Myclobutanil 40% WP @ 0.5g per litre of water.
Mancozeb 75% WP applied prior to bloom.

pathogen: Pseudocercospora clavispora (Fungus causing dark angular leaf spots)
symptoms: Dark brown angular necrotic spots bounded by leaf veins.
Leaves turn dry, brittle, and drop prematurely in late summer.
causes: High humidity, poor airflow through the trellis, and dense foliage.
spread: Spores spread by wind and rain splash during humid late summer.
preventive_measures: Thin the vine canopy to allow sunlight and wind penetration.
organic_treatments: Apply 1% Bordeaux mixture post-harvest.
chemical_controls: Azoxystrobin @ 1 mL per litre or Carbendazim @ 1g per litre.

pathogen: Magnaporthe oryzae (Fungus causing spindle-shaped blast lesions)
symptoms: Spindle-shaped spots with gray or white centers and brown-red borders appear on leaves.
Spots enlarge and join together, causing whole rice leaves to dry up.
Can attack the neck of the rice panicle, causing empty white grains.
causes: Excessive use of nitrogen fertilizer.
High humidity above 90% with night temperatures around 20°C.
spread: Fungal spores blown in the wind settle on moist rice leaves.
preventive_measures: Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizer; split doses and use silicon supplements.
Maintain continuous shallow water in paddy fields.
Use certified blast-resistant rice seed varieties.
organic_treatments: Treat seeds with Pseudomonas fluorescens bio-inoculant @ 10g per kg seed.
Apply silicon fertilizers to strengthen rice leaf cell walls.
chemical_controls: Tricyclazole 75% WP @ 0.6g per litre of water.
Isoprothiolane 40% EC @ 1.5 mL per litre.

pathogen: Bipolaris oryzae (Fungus causing oval brown spots on leaves)
symptoms: Small oval dark brown spots resembling sesame seeds appear on leaves.
A yellow ring surrounds each dark brown spot.
Heavy spotting leads to poor grain filling and discolored seeds.
causes: Nutrient-poor soil (especially low potassium, silicon, or manganese).
Drought stress or uneven water levels in the paddy field.
spread: Infected seeds and wind-carried spores spread the disease across fields.
preventive_measures: Correct soil potash and micronutrient deficiencies before planting.
Ensure steady water levels during tillering and flowering stages.
organic_treatments: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4g per kg seed.
chemical_controls: Propiconazole 25% EC @ 1 mL per litre of water.
Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g per litre.

causes: Balanced nutrients, proper water management, and healthy seedlings.
spread: Not applicable (healthy plant).
preventive_measures: Maintain integrated nutrient management and weed control.

pathogen: Xanthomonas campestris (Bacterium that causes water-soaked spots with yellow halos)
symptoms: Small water-soaked dark brown spots appear on leaves.
Spots have visible yellow edges and cause leaves to look scorched.
Heavily spotted leaves drop off, exposing pepper fruits to sunburn.
Rough brown blister-like warts may develop on pepper fruits.
causes: Warm temperatures (24–30°C) with driving rain or overhead sprinkler watering.
Contaminated seeds or infected plant residue in the soil.
spread: Bacteria splash easily from leaf to leaf in water droplets during rain or sprinkler irrigation.
preventive_measures: Use certified disease-free pepper seeds.
Avoid overhead irrigation; use drip irrigation under plastic mulch.
Rotate crops away from solanaceous plants for at least 2 years.
organic_treatments: Apply copper-based bactericides combined with Bacillus subtilis.
Hot-water seed treatment before sowing.
chemical_controls: Copper hydroxide + Mancozeb tank mix @ 2g each per litre of water.

pathogen: Pythium / Fusarium / Rhizoctonia (Soil fungi that cause root decay)
symptoms: Roots turn dark brown or black, becoming soft, water-soaked, and decayed.
Outer root layer easily peels away, leaving only thin thread-like inner root.
Very few healthy white feeder root tips remain.
Above ground, the plant wilts, turns yellow, and collapses even if soil is wet.
causes: Poor soil drainage, persistent waterlogging, and compacted wet soil.
Soil-borne fungal molds multiplying in stagnant wet conditions.
spread: Soil molds spread through stagnant drainage water and contaminated gardening tools.
preventive_measures: Improve soil drainage using raised planting beds or adding organic compost.
Allow the top soil layer to dry out slightly between waterings.
Ensure nursery pots have clear, open drainage holes.
organic_treatments: Drench roots with beneficial Trichoderma harzianum bio-fungicide @ 10g per litre.
Apply Bacillus subtilis root drench at transplanting time.
chemical_controls: Metalaxyl 35% WS root drench @ 2g per litre of water.
Carbendazim + Mancozeb (Saaf) root drench @ 2.5g per litre.

Many fine root hairs and active white growing root tips.
Clean earthy scent without any unpleasant rot odor or soft mushy areas.
causes: Well-drained aerated soil, balanced watering, and healthy soil biology.
